# Results — Study 302 (Lithium-Boom) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The canonical **time-series-trend
overlay** — hold the asset when its close is above its own 200-day moving average, else sit in
cash; signal at the close of *t* held over *t+1* (one `shift`) — run on **LIT** (Global X
Lithium & Battery Tech) and two pure-play miners **ALB**, **SQM**, with **SPY** as the
benchmark. Total-return (`auto_adjust=True`) daily bars. Pinned against **buy-and-hold the same
asset** (raced excess-of-cash Sharpe vs excess-of-cash Sharpe, rf = 1.5%/yr) and a
**random-timing control** (same exposure budget, random days). Costs **10 bps one-way on NAV**
per flip unless noted. As-of **2026-06-17**; match the per-tape fingerprint to confirm you hold
the same tape.*

## The headline — LIT, 200-day trend overlay vs buy-and-hold

| Book | CAGR | excess Sharpe | max DD | HAC *t* (excess ret) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| LIT buy-and-hold (total-return) | +7.5% | 0.34 | **−66%** | +1.36 |
| Trend overlay, gross | +10.4% | 0.55 | −39% | +2.24 |
| **Trend overlay, net (10 bps/flip)** | **+9.7%** | **0.51** | **−41%** | **+2.09** |

- The net trend overlay clears the inference bar: HAC *t* = **+2.09** on its excess-of-cash
  daily returns (gross +2.24), so the in-market exposure earns a return distinguishable from
  zero — a **REAL** signal on the real tape.
- The overlay roughly **halves the worst drawdown** (−66% → −41%) and lifts excess Sharpe
  (0.34 → 0.51 net), trading ~6.5 one-way flips/yr while ~43% invested.

## The honest pin — does the *timing* beat buy-and-hold?

The overlay sits in cash part of the time, so we race **excess-of-cash Sharpe vs
excess-of-cash Sharpe**, and we test the daily **difference** (Trend − B&H) directly:

| Asset | B&H excess-Sharpe | Trend net excess-Sharpe | (Trend − B&H) daily diff, ann. | diff HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| LIT | 0.34 | 0.51 | −0.33%/yr | **−0.06** |
| ALB | — | 0.43 | — | −0.76 |
| SQM | — | 0.39 | — | −0.55 |

The difference HAC *t* is **≈ 0 (slightly negative)** on all three names. The overlay does
**not** add return; it **swaps return for risk reduction**. The block-bootstrap 95% CI for the
LIT trend Sharpe is **[0.02, 0.99]** — it barely clears zero and overlaps B&H's CI **[−0.17,
0.85]** almost entirely, so the Sharpe *improvement* is not statistically distinguishable.

## The timing-skill control — same exposure, random days

Replace the trend signal with a random 0/1 path of the *same* average exposure:

| Asset | Trend net Sharpe | Random-timing net Sharpe (mean of 200) | Trend's percentile vs random |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| LIT | 0.51 | −0.45 | **100th** |
| ALB | 0.43 | −0.09 | **100th** |
| SQM | 0.39 | −0.14 | **100th** |

Random timing is a disaster (you buy the dips that keep dipping). The trend rule sits at the
**100th percentile** of random timing on every name — the *when* genuinely carried
information. That information is overwhelmingly about **stepping aside during the crash leg**,
which is where the drawdown reduction comes from.

## Context — the sleeve trails the index it concentrates away from

| Book | Sharpe (excess of cash) |
|---|--:|
| LIT trend overlay, net | 0.51 |
| **SPY buy-and-hold** | **0.77** |
| SPY trend overlay, net | 0.76 |

You took on single-theme battery-metals concentration and the best trend version (LIT, 0.51)
still earns **worse risk-adjusted returns than simply holding the S&P 500** (0.77).

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is a faithful trend detector

On a deterministic synthetic tape carrying the *same* boom-bust envelope but a tunable AR(1)
persistence, the overlay's Sharpe edge over B&H appears **only when persistence is planted**;
the drawdown reduction is present even on a pure random walk (it is a property of the long/flat
structure, not evidence of skill):

| Planted `trend_strength` | B&H Sharpe (DD) | Trend net Sharpe (DD) | Sharpe edge | diff HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (random walk) | 0.40 (−86%) | 0.38 (−61%) | −0.02 | −0.69 |
| 0.05 | 0.41 (−87%) | 0.51 (−58%) | +0.10 | −0.20 |
| 0.10 | 0.42 (−88%) | 0.51 (−60%) | +0.09 | −0.27 |
| 0.15 | 0.43 (−89%) | 0.55 (−57%) | +0.12 | −0.16 |

At zero persistence the Sharpe edge vanishes while the drawdown still drops — the cleanest
proof that *cutting the drawdown is not the same as adding skill*.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** LIT net trend overlay HAC *t* = +2.09 (gross +2.24), and the trend timing beats a
  random-timing control of identical exposure at the 100th percentile on all three names. The
  *when* carries information (mostly: get out before the crash).
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Net Sharpe ~0.5 with a bootstrap CI [0.02, 0.99] that barely
  clears zero; a single thin thematic sleeve that trails plain SPY (0.77). The edge is risk
  reduction, not return, and it is statistically thin.
- **Did riding the boom pay? — MISATTRIBUTED.** The believer's pitch is *boom-riding return*;
  what the overlay actually delivers is *crash-dodging drawdown reduction* — the (Trend − B&H)
  return difference is HAC *t* ≈ 0 (−0.06). It halved the drawdown; it added no return.
